decision: Started the Omarchy-on-niri port in rbelem/nix-config
why: the task touches the compositor, the desktop and the packaging

decision: Target: the Omarchy desktop on niri, plus a niri fork that implements the GlobalShortcuts portal
why: the request named both the desktop and the missing portal support

decision: Read nixarchy to find out how deeply Omarchy couples to Hyprland
why: nixarchy was given as the reference, so its shape decides what can be reused
result: found: 99 of 536 bin scripts and 33 of 249 shell files reference Hyprland

decision: Checked niri issues for an existing GlobalShortcuts implementation
why: writing the portal from scratch is expensive if someone already did

decision: Implement the portal the way KDE does, not the way niri PR 3587 does
why: PR 3587 goes through xdg-desktop-portal-gnome and needs a config entry per app and shortcut id; KDE implements the compositor-side interface directly and binds dynamically

decision: Port Omarchy's keybindings by hand instead of reusing the upstream Lua
why: Hyprland's Lua API and IPC have no niri equivalent, so there is nothing to reuse

decision: Replace the QuickShell bar and menu with a fuzzel launcher
why: the shell imports Quickshell.Hyprland and there is no niri module for it

decision: Keep the niri fork as a patch file in this repository
why: a patch against the nixpkgs-pinned v26.04 stays reviewable and needs no network at build time

decision: Gate Plasma on programs.omarchy.enable so both desktops stay switchable
why: the laptop ran Plasma; removing it outright would take away a working setup

decision: Validated the generated niri configuration with niri itself
why: a config that niri rejects is a broken desktop

decision: Ported the Omarchy keybindings to niri actions by hand
why: Hyprland's Lua API has no niri counterpart, so each binding needed a semantic decision rather than a transliteration

decision: Fixed the workspace binds to niri's argument form
why: niri validate rejected focus-workspace-1; the real syntax is focus-workspace 1

decision: Dropped the vertical window swaps
why: niri scrolls sideways, so swap-window-up and swap-window-down do not exist

decision: Limited the workspace number binds to 1 through 9
why: niri has no two digit key name, so Super+10 does not parse

decision: Pointed the session at the generated config through NIRI_CONFIG
why: niri-session does not forward arguments to niri, but niri reads NIRI_CONFIG and niri-session imports the environment into the user manager

decision: Gave the desktop its own greeter through SDDM
why: Plasma's login manager lives in the Plasma module, which is off while the Omarchy desktop is on

decision: Made the terminal, browser, editor and file manager package options
why: the keybindings launch them, so the binary has to exist in the session PATH

decision: Confirmed the zet configuration still evaluates
why: the desktop change touches shared flake wiring

decision: Confirmed the rt-ax88u failure is pre-existing
why: the same error appears on the unmodified HEAD, so it is not from this change

decision: Used the existing rbelem/niri fork for the patch branch
why: the fork already existed on GitHub, so the patch goes there instead of creating a new repository

decision: Checked every vendored theme parses and carries the keys the terminal themes read
why: a theme without a key would break the module for anyone who selects it

decision: Built the fork derivation against a placeholder patch
why: the patch file, the cargo lock and the portal file install all had to line up before the real patch arrived

decision: Built the fork derivation against a placeholder patch
why: the patch file, the cargo lock and the portal file install all had to line up before the real patch arrived

decision: Installed the portal backend as a file, not a directory
why: install -t treats its target as a directory, so niri.portal came out as a directory holding the file

decision: Recorded that nix flake check already fails on the unmodified checkout
why: the check has to be run on its own, otherwise a pre-existing failure hides the result
evidence: nix flake check --no-build on git archive HEAD
result: pre-existing: ASUS GPL source not available

decision: Checked how libxkbcommon resolves a letter key name, because the portal trigger has to match what niri sees
why: xkb_keysym_from_name with CASE_INSENSITIVE returns the lower-case keysym, and niri binds on the raw keysym, so the portal parser and the input hook must agree on which keysym they compare
result: confirmed: the case-insensitive lookup returns the lower-case keysym

decision: Ran an independent review of the Nix side against Omarchy upstream and niri
why: the work was mine alone, so a second seat was needed
result: review found three runtime breaks and several undisclosed changes

decision: Wrote the terminal main configuration as well as the colours
why: the theme was written but nothing loaded it, so the terminals stayed at their defaults

decision: Rendered the ghostty theme as hex instead of decimal triplets
why: ghostty's RGB.parse takes hex, an X11 name or rgb:r/g/b, and never r,g,b

decision: Rendered the foot theme in the colors-dark and colors-light sections without a hash
why: foot 1.28 moved its colours out of a colors section and wants bare hex digits

decision: Moved the alacritty import into the general section
why: alacritty deprecated the top level import key

decision: Pointed the catalogue at code-cursor and dropped the Languages entries from the launcher
why: pkgs.cursor does not exist, and a language runtime cannot be launched as a window

decision: Added the tenth workspace, the vertical monitor moves and the resize binds
why: niri has all three, and Omarchy binds them

decision: Corrected the recon row: the counts came from omarchy, not nixarchy
why: the row attached omarchy's numbers to nixarchy's files, which is wrong even though the conclusion held
result: corrected: nixarchy has no bin directory; the counts are omarchy's

decision: Put the verification in the flake as checks.omarchy-desktop instead of a script
why: a reviewer has to be able to re-run the check with one command

decision: Kept the app catalogue declarative rather than a menu that edits the configuration
why: Omarchy's install menu writes a declaration; in a NixOS configuration the declaration is the configuration

decision: Checked the rendered theme against the terminals themselves
why: every terminal has its own colour format and fails silently when it is wrong
result: foot, alacritty, kitty and ghostty all read the theme

decision: Pushed the portal branch to the existing rbelem/niri fork
why: the user asked for a fork of niri, and the fork was already there to push to

decision: Kept the fork as four patches against niri v26.04
why: one patch per commit keeps the difference against upstream readable and lets the build apply them in order

decision: Read the fork's own report and checked its claims against the tree
why: the lane reported 201 niri tests and 23 config tests passing; the tree shows the same four commits and an unchanged Cargo.lock

decision: Built the fork from the four patch files
why: the patch has to apply to the revision nixpkgs pins, and the cargo lock has to stay untouched
result: builds, portal backend and D-Bus service installed

decision: Ran the desktop check end to end
why: the check is the proof that the desktop holds together
result: passes: portal backend, interface, config parses, session offered, backend preferred, four terminals read the theme
